focus: Phases 004-computer-exposure and 005-memory: which reference files implement the same thing, what a builder should lift or mirror, where the plan differs from the reference and which side the evidence supports, and which failures the plan does not yet guard against.
noveltyJustification: All 9 findings are new to the packet; 2 of them confirm a plan rule the reference reached independently rather than reporting a gap.
ruledOut: Reading computer-control.ts as 004 reference implementation: the plan excludes the browser computer
Porting tinymemory engine or namespace tree into 005: the plan two files and one bound are the right size
A three-state memory key as a gap: the plan boolean is right for a file with no inheritance chain

graphEvents.label: Which reference files implement computer exposure and memory
Computer means a browser container in the reference and a working place in the plan
The reference auto-approves a memory proposal and the plan raises a needs-you item

findings.label: 004: computer means a browser container with a durable handoff in the reference and a working place in the plan, and the plan is right to exclude it but 013 must not let the phase name read as the computer.

004: the reference re-checks the world on a resume through resumeSnapshotRequired and the plan refuses the resume, and the plan answer is the cheaper one because a file-backed run has no page to re-check.
004: the reference has a restart-recovery rule, keepsPage set only on a request a restart interrupted, and the plan covers a resume and a refused run but nothing about a runtime restart.

005: the reference memory is a token-budgeted context.md compile and the plan 60-entry 3600-byte bound is the same idea at a smaller scale, so the plan should cite the compile idea and not port an engine.
005: the reference fixes memory scope at the host and the plan does the same independently, which is the strongest evidence in this phase that the rule is right.
005: the reference ships a conformance suite and an in-memory reference engine and the plan has neither, and 012 should own that pattern for the two bounded stores in 005 and 008.

005: the reference per-bot memory setting is three-state, missing inherits and null excludes, while the plan key is a boolean, which is right for a file with no inheritance chain and should be recorded with that condition.

005: the reference approves a memory proposal without review by default and the plan raises a needs-you item, and the plan is right because a memory entry is read into every later prompt as an operator-confirmed fact.
005: the plan closes the bot-writes-memory hole the reference leaves open by refusing the write forms under the child marker, and that refusal is the one line a builder must not drop.
